title: fine-grained-kernel-latency-mapping-and-span-tagging
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Add low-overhead, fine-grained mapping from GPU kernel dispatches to runtime trace spans and NVTX ranges so we can attribute per-kernel latency to request-level prefill/decode spans. Current telemetry captures coarse-span timings and occasional NVTX markers but lacks a reliable, low-noise join between kernel-level timers and the distributed tracing system. This ticket will design and implement a light-weight correlation mechanism, per-kernel histogram collection, and tagging of trace spans with dominant kernels and skewed latency signals.
context_and_problem: Operators and SREs frequently see elevated tail latency for text-generation workloads but cannot determine whether the bottleneck is kernel selection, a specific attention kernel, or scheduling behavior during prefill vs decode. Existing NVTX ranges are useful but inconsistent across backend code paths and they do not contain kernel implementation metadata or batch/seq length attributes. Kernel-level CUDA events are too noisy when naively recorded for every dispatch, and existing per-kernel counters are aggregated at coarse frequency, making spike attribution difficult.
proposed_solution: 1) Introduce a small correlation token injected into NVTX ranges and trace spans at dispatch-time (span_token = <request_id>:<phase>:<step_index>). 2) At kernel enqueuing, emit a compact kernel telemetry record (timestamp_ns host_enq, kernel_name, kernel_impl, batch_size, seq_len, device_stream_id, span_token) into a lock-free ring-buffer shared with a background collector thread. 3) Background collector aggregates per-kernel histograms (p50/p90/p99), per-phase aggregates (prefill/decode), and top-k slowest kernel occurrences, and periodically flushes to telemetry backend (Prometheus/OTLP) as aggregated metrics with labels. 4) Enrich OTel spans with top_kernel and top_kernel_latency_ms for the span when available, and add a span attribute kernel_count>threshold for anomaly detection. 5) Provide a sampling mode (1/N or deterministic tail-sampling) to limit overhead for high-throughput nodes.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime emits compact kernel telemetry records without blocking hot-path (background collector reports flush success)
Aggregated Prometheus metrics created: runtime_kernel_latency_ms_bucket, runtime_kernel_count_total with labels (kernel_name, kernel_impl, phase, seq_len_bucket, batch_size_bucket)
OTel spans for prefill/decode contain top_kernel and top_kernel_latency_ms attributes when latency > 95th percentile observed for that span type
End-to-end dashboard shows per-model and per-route kernel contribution slices and can filter by phase and seq_len
Overhead measured in microbenchmark: <3% median latency increase and <8% tail increase when sampling disabled; <0.5% median when sampling 1/10
Design doc and implementation PR reviewed by Runtime and Observability teams and merged behind feature flag runtime.kernel_telemetry_v2
implementation_notes: Place minimal serialization logic in hot path: build fixed-size 64B record in thread-local buffer, then push index into ring buffer
Background collector runs on a dedicated CPU core, performs batch reads and computes HDR histograms per kernel+phase
Bucketize seq_len and batch_size into defined ranges (seq_len: 1-16,17-64,65-256,>256; batch_size:1,2-8,9-32,>32) to limit label cardinality
Use existing NVTX helper to annotate ranges but avoid repeated NVTX pushes for micro-kernels; instead annotate only span boundaries and rely on span_token for correlation
Expose runtime flags: telemetry.enable, telemetry.sampling_rate, telemetry.flush_interval_ms, telemetry.max_ring_capacity
Instrumentation points: kernel_dispatcher.cpp (enqueue), runtime_span_manager (when creating prefill/decode spans), collector thread in runtime/telemetry
telemetry_queries: BigQuery sample join: SELECT span_id, top_kernel, top_kernel_latency_ms FROM traces WHERE resource.labels.model_id='redwood-7b' AND span.name LIKE '%prefill%' ORDER BY top_kernel_latency_ms DESC LIMIT 100
Alert example: IF increase(runtime_kernel_count_total{kernel_name="kv_cache_write"}[5m]) > 100 AND histogram_quantile(0.95, rate(runtime_kernel_latency_ms_bucket[5m])) > 50 THEN fire PagerDuty
dashboards_and_visuals: New dashboard: Kernel Contribution Explorer - per-model breakdown with stacked bars showing cumulative kernel time per request phase
Span Driller: trace view with annotated top_kernel attributes and link to kernel histogram for that trace window
Heatmap: seq_len vs kernel latency for top 10 kernels over 24h window
progress_updates: 2025-02-12: Spike completed. Implemented a micro-prototype that writes 64B records to an mmaped ring buffer and a collector that aggregates HDR histograms. Measured overhead ~2.6% median on toy workload.
2025-02-20: Design review with Observability team. Agreed on label bucketing and that only aggregated metrics will be exported to Prometheus to reduce cardinality.
2025-02-25: Prototype PR created (see links). CI tests failing on Windows builds due to mmap usage; added fallback to lock-free queue implementation.
2025-03-01: Internal perf run against real workload. Found heavy tail caused by collector flush blocking writer under high concurrency; implementing per-thread buffering to reduce contention.
2025-03-04: Preparing implementation PR for review. Feature behind runtime.kernel_telemetry_v2 flag. Need final signoff from Security on exported labels (ensure no PII).
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: High cardinality labels leading to Prometheus blowup. Mitigation: enforce static buckets for seq_len/batch_size and cap unique kernel_impl labels.
Risk: Collector introduces CPU spike during flush. Mitigation: background collector backpressure, adaptive flush window, and shard collectors by device.
Risk: Correlation token may leak customer identifiers. Mitigation: use internal-only opaque span_token and hash sensitive IDs before emission
